mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Captur 1.5 dCi engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fully rebuilt K9K engine for a Renault Captur 1.5 dCi typically costs £1,200-£2,200 supply-only or £1,800-£3,000 fitted. Used units start from £400, and reconditioned options sit between £900-£1,700. Blue dCi variants (K9K 872, K9K 873) are slightly higher at £1,500-£2,600. K9K 609 and K9K 628 (90hp) are the cheapest to replace - £1,200-£2,000. K9K 646 and K9K 856 (110hp) are £1,400-£2,200. K9K 873 (115hp Blue dCi) is the most expensive - £1,600-£2,600. All EnginesMarket quotes include 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF and EGR problems on a Captur 1.5 dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs include: a "Check Anti-Pollution System" warning, a "Check Injection" message, loss of power during acceleration, increased fuel consumption, and difficulty starting. DPF issues are common on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys. EGR valve carbon buildup is the most frequent cause of "Check Anti-Pollution" warnings. A forced DPF regeneration (£100-£200) is often the first step in diagnosis.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Renault Captur 1.5 dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2013-2015 Captur 1.5 dCi worth £2,500-£5,000, a £1,800-£3,000 engine replacement is borderline unless the vehicle is in exceptional condition with low mileage. For vehicles worth over £3,500, replacement is typically viable if the rest of the car is sound. The 1.5 dCi is a durable engine when timing belt and injector maintenance are kept up. Compare the cost of a rebuilt unit with warranty vs. buying another used Captur. We always recommend a specialist inspection before any decision.

mainEntity.name: How reliable is the Renault Captur 1.5 dCi engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The K9K 1.5 dCi is generally considered one of the most durable diesel engines in its class - but it has predictable maintenance requirements. DPF and EGR issues are common (60k-100k miles), injector seal leaks are known to occur, and timing belt replacement at 37,000 miles (60,000km) is non-negotiable. The engine is used across Renault, Nissan, Mercedes, and other brands - proven reliability record. Regular motorway driving helps prevent DPF clogging. Timing belt neglect is the single biggest cause of catastrophic failure.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Renault Captur 1.5 dCi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full engine replacement on a Captur 1.5 dCi typically takes 2-3 working days for a specialist (3-5 days for a main dealer). Timing belt replacement is 1-2 days. DPF/EGR cleaning is typically a 1-day job. Injector seal replacement is 1-2 days. Supply & fit providers may offer courtesy vehicle options.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 1.5 dCi and the 1.5 Blue dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5 dCi (2013-2019) is the first-generation diesel engine, available in 90hp and 110hp variants. The 1.5 Blue dCi (2020-present) is the updated second-generation engine, available in 95hp and 115hp variants, with improved emissions technology including AdBlue. The Blue dCi has a revised ECU calibration and updated emissions systems but shares the same K9K engine family and 1,461cc displacement. Blue dCi variants have AdBlue systems that require regular top-ups. The Blue dCi 115 (K9K 873) is the most powerful Captur diesel available. When replacing, ensure the replacement engine matches your vehicle's generation.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Captur 1.5 dCi & Blue dCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 1.5 dCi diesel engine - part of Renault's widely used K9K family - was available in the Renault Captur from launch in 2013. It proved to be the most popular diesel choice for UK buyers, offering a combination of strong fuel economy, decent torque, and low running costs for family and fleet use. The engine was offered in two power outputs - 90hp and 110hp - across the first-generation Captur (2013-2019). From 2020, the second-generation Captur introduced the updated 1.5 Blue dCi with emissions improvements and power outputs of 95hp and 115hp.

milestones.description: Captur launched; K9K 608 (90hp) and K9K 609 (90hp) introduced
K9K 646 (110hp) introduced, offering 20hp more than the 90hp unit
Second-generation Captur launched; 1.5 Blue dCi introduced with K9K 872 (95hp) and K9K 873 (115hp)
Blue dCi continues with updated emissions calibration

commonProblems.h2: Renault Captur 1.5 dCi & Blue dCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 1.5 dCi (K9K family) is one of the most common diesel engines in the UK - and while it's generally reliable, predictable issues emerge with age and mileage. DPF clogging, EGR valve failure, injector seal leaks, and timing belt wear dominate replacement discussions. Rebuilt 1.5 dCi engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded emissions components and new timing belts, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF and EGR System Clogging - Why the Renault Captur 1.5 dCi Suffers Emission System Issues
problems.affectedModels: Renault Captur 1.5 dCi and Blue dCi (all K9K variants, 2013-present)
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 60,000-100,000 miles (urban use vehicles may fail earlier)
problems.rootCause: The Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) becomes blocked on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys where regeneration cycles are not completed. The EGR valve also accumulates carbon deposits, restricting airflow. Symptoms include a "Check Anti-Pollution System" warning, "Check Injection" messages, loss of power, and increased fuel consumption. A 2016 recall affected 15,000 Captur units for EGR valve calibration.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if DPF is partially blocked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: DPF removal and cleaning, EGR valve replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if both systems are affected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt K9K with new DPF and EGR
repairOptions.longevity: If DPF/EGR failure has caused turbo or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2013-2019 Renault Captur 1.5 dCi is worth £2,500-£8,000 depending on year, mileage, and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. DPF/EGR cleaning (£300-£600) is well within value for any running example. A full engine replacement (£1,800-£3,000) is viable for vehicles worth £3,500+, but for sub-£2,500 examples, evaluate scrap value before committing to a full rebuild.
problems.recommendation: DPF and EGR issues are the most common reason for engine-related warnings on the 1.5 dCi. If you use your Captur primarily for short urban journeys, ensure regular motorway runs to allow DPF regeneration. If you see a "Check Anti-Pollution System" warning, get a diagnostic immediately - a £100-£200 forced regeneration is far cheaper than a full DPF replacement.

problems.h4: Injector Seal Leakage - Fuel System Issues on the Captur 1.5 dCi
problems.affectedModels: Renault Captur 1.5 dCi (K9K 609, K9K 628, K9K 646, K9K 856, 2013-2019)
problems.rootCause: The injector seals can leak, causing combustion gases to escape past the injectors. This leads to a "diesel knock" sound, "Check Injection" warnings, and in severe cases, fuel dilution of engine oil. Symptoms include a knocking noise from the engine, diesel smell in the cabin, and hard starting. Injector seal leaks can also cause the fuel rail pressure sensor to report low pressure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New copper seals, injector cleaning, leak-off test
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; injectors not seized

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Seized injectors removed, new injectors and seals
repairOptions.longevity: If injectors have seized in the cylinder head

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt K9K with new injectors and seals
repairOptions.longevity: If injector failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Injector seal replacement (£350-£600) is well within value for any Captur 1.5 dCi worth £2,000+. If injectors are seized and the vehicle is worth under £2,500, evaluate whether a used engine (£400-£700) plus fitting is more cost-effective than a full rebuild.
problems.recommendation: Injector seal leaks are a maintenance item that should be addressed promptly. If you have a Captur 1.5 dCi with 60,000+ miles and no injector service history, budget for seal replacement. A "diesel knock" sound should never be ignored - it indicates combustion gas leakage and can lead to injector seizure.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt K9K 609 Renault Captur 1.5 dCi engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Belt Replacement - Critical Maintenance on the Captur 1.5 dCi
problems.affectedModels: Renault Captur 1.5 dCi and Blue dCi (all K9K variants, 2013-present)
problems.rootCause: The 1.5 dCi K9K engine uses a timing belt, not a chain. The belt must be replaced at the recommended interval to prevent catastrophic engine failure. Symptoms of impending failure include rattling or squeaking noises from the front of the engine on cold start, and visible cracking on the belt surface. Belt failure on this interference engine causes piston-to-valve contact and severe engine damage. Some owners report belt failure at 40,000 miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Belt, tensioner, idler pulley, water pump replacement
Cylinder head rebuild with new valves, guides
repairOptions.longevity: If belt has snapped but bottom end is undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt K9K with new timing components
repairOptions.longevity: If belt failure has caused bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Timing belt replacement (£350-£600) is a routine maintenance cost - it's well within value for any Captur 1.5 dCi. For vehicles with a snapped belt, the repair cost (£1,500-£2,500) may approach the value of sub-£2,500 examples.
problems.recommendation: Do not skip the timing belt service. The 60,000km (37,000-mile) interval is non-negotiable on an interference engine. If you don't have documented belt history on a used Captur 1.5 dCi, budget for immediate replacement - the cost is far lower than the alternative. Some specialists recommend replacement at 5 years regardless of mileage.
